name: One baseline per device
summary: Every check that ever passed is held to; a check outside a run's scope is not asked, rather than kept in a second baseline.
why: Two baselines would be two truths about one phone.

name: The conveyor refuses what cannot work
summary: Each mistake that cost a try becomes a refusal with a reason: a kernel that is not an EFI program, a listening test without the word that the microphone is placed.
why: A refusal costs a second; a lost try costs a reboot and a wrong theory.

name: Read the device's own record first
summary: Before cleaning up after an experiment, read what the device itself recorded: a boot entry's try counter, the bootloader's selection, the crash memory.
why: Three theories about the bootloader were wrong; the entry's counter settled it in one look.

name: A placed microphone gives relative levels
summary: A microphone placed by the phone tells which speaker is louder from where it stands, and whether there is sound at all - not absolute loudness.
why: Honest about what the instrument can say.

name: The phone is the reference
summary: Kept in a known-working state at all times: every experiment is one try that falls back by itself, and the phone is checked well before and after.
why: A reference that drifts cannot tell a regression from a mistake.

name: As good as Android
summary: A phone running Linux that an ordinary person could use as their only phone and not feel they gave something up - counted one feature at a time.
why: The aim is plain and counted against Android's everyday use (the idea, section 05); without a measure it would be a hope.

name: Measured, not claimed
summary: A feature counts only when a test run has shown it works; what nobody measured is unknown, never broken.
why: The picture is honest or it is worth nothing: status is read off the runs (decision 2026-11-17-support-read-off-results).

name: Mainline first, everything upstream
summary: Work is done on mainline Linux and written to be sent upstream: each fix its own series, checkpatch-clean, to the upstream it belongs to; vendor code is read as a specification, never copied.
why: A fix kept in a fork helps one phone; a fix upstream helps every phone and stays maintained.

name: No manual steps outside tools
summary: What a person does twice becomes a command, a record or a test, so that bringing a phone up can run by itself; where hands or eyes are the measurement, the step is a witnessed test, said before and recorded.
why: The conveyor's point (the idea, section 03): the same known steps every time, by a person or an agent; manual_work counts what is still by hand and whether it is automated.

name: Rust, with argenv
summary: linux-phone's tools are Rust, each declaring its command line and environment once with argenv.
why: One declaration gives the parser, the help, the man page and the completions, so they cannot disagree.

name: A structure that explains itself
summary: Anyone, a person or an agent, knows where a thing is and why just by looking: one meaning per top-level folder with a README saying it, a short map at the top of every README, branch names that say whose and what, one home per kind of thing, and checks that refuse a thing in the wrong home.
why: The author, 2026-11-22: "currently all our repositories are a damn mess, agents create folders in root folder without trying to group them, to make sense of them, and without making them selfinformative, so that anyone humans or agents could make sense of it and know where things are just by looking at the structure." A place chosen by whoever creates the thing, with nothing tying it to a session or ending it, is how the mess grew (research structure-review-what-is).
